local_checks.invariant: The lock gate re-engages after the grace period and cannot be shortened by anything outside the app
local_checks.result: Grace period is measured with Date() (wall clock) at AppScreen.swift:95 (set), :162 and :174 (compared). The lockout, by contrast, is anchored on monotonic uptime (Manager+Security.swift:35-36, 650-666) precisely because Date & Time changes must not matter. A backward clock change makes elapsed negative or small, so the gate stays open. Single scene only (UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes false), one AppScreen. Candidate secure-mode:appscreen-grace-period-uses-wall-clock.

local_checks.invariant: Nothing renders before the PIN on cold launch, warm return, or a lowered gate
local_checks.result: Cold launch: phase .covered renders Color.clear (OccultaApp.swift:384-386); wire() runs after first render (:277-278); with a PIN, evaluate(coldLaunch:true) goes to .pinRequired. Lowered gate: Manager.Security.init restores currentDepth from persistedDepth only when pinEnabled is false (Manager+Security.swift:255-258), so no stale depth is shown. Warm return: lockIfGracePeriodExpired runs in sceneWillEnterForeground before URL delivery (AppScreen.swift:158-165). Every sheet/alert/cover is attached inside the .unlocked branch (OccultaApp.swift:410-535), so none renders over PINEntry. currentDepth is not reset on lock, but nothing outside the .unlocked branch reads it for display; the gated sweeps check phase == .unlocked (:957, :968). Holds apart from the wall-clock grace candidate and the hardening notes.

local_checks.invariant: State held above the unlocked tree is ended when the session ends or the depth changes in place
local_checks.result: endSession (OccultaApp.swift:563-579) runs on leaving .unlocked (:315) and on sessionID change (:337); the unlocked tree is keyed by sessionID (:536). It clears opened file, share result, restore prompt state, error flag, identity challenge presentations, card import, open request, and locks the vault. pendingFileData, pendingShareSession and selectedTab survive by design (:220-251). Vault lock also fires on background/resign-active (Vault+Manager.swift:196-208). The one in-place depth change that needs no PIN is deactivateSecureMode (Manager+Security.swift:446-505), which is candidate secure-mode:deactivate-at-coercer-base-depth-pops-to-depth0.

local_checks.invariant: A depth transition toward depth 0 requires depth 0's PIN
local_checks.result: Traced coercer at depth 1 holding only P1: Settings shows Learn more at state .duress (Settings.swift:237); activateSecureMode(confirming P1) is valid from depth>0 and writes coercerBaseDepth = depth (Manager+Security.swift:400-428); then isAtSecureModeHomeDepth is true at depth 1 (Settings.swift:202-207); Deactivate confirms against normal[1] = P1 and does newDepth = max(0, depth-1) = 0 with setState (:487-495), clearing the owner's depth 0-to-1 verifiers. Candidate secure-mode:deactivate-at-coercer-base-depth-pops-to-depth0.

hardening: AppScreen.sceneDidBecomeActive (AppScreen.swift:104-111) removes the UIKit cover whenever phase == .pinRequired, assuming PINEntry is already on screen; lockIfGracePeriodExpired sets .pinRequired in the earlier sceneWillEnterForeground, so if SwiftUI has not yet committed PINEntry the unlocked frame can show once. Validate on device; pinViewAppeared is the right sole remover.

The snapshot cover installs only if a duress verifier exists (isSecureModeActive, AppScreen.swift:84-90); with a PIN but no Secure Mode the app-switcher snapshot and the warm-return frame show live content. Related to known FTA U5d.

Manager.Security.requiresPIN and the gate in evaluate()/lockIfGracePeriodExpired read config with try?; a failed fetch evaluates as no PIN and unlocks. Fail closed on a fetch error (Manager+Security.swift:78-81).

IdentityChallenge.Coordinator.approvePending (Coordinator.swift:262-312) sets outboundShare after a biometric await with no sessionEpoch check; endSession cannot cancel it. Narrow because backgrounding cancels the prompt; add an epoch or phase check like processInboundFile.
UIPasteboard.copySensitive content (120 s) is not cleared by endSession, so text copied at one depth is readable after a lock or depth change within the window; extends known FTA O2.
pendingFileData is a single slot (OccultaApp.swift:220, 743-746): a second file delivered while locked replaces the first, whose source copy has already been deleted. Availability only.

Pre-PIN work at launch (LaunchSequence, sweepExpired, checkpointStore, cleanupPendingSessions) takes no depth input; its failures lead only to the StorageErrorView for every depth, which shows no depth-dependent text.
purgeOrphanedGroupsIfAtRealDepth does extra reads only at depth 0 (OccultaApp.swift:955-962); the checkpoint is unconditional, so no write-pattern difference was found.

local_checks.invariant: An inbound .occ (1:1, group, streamed, legacy) opened at depth N reads the depth only where a documented decision says so; the sender-resolve, slot-open, prekey-consume, replenish and persist steps are identical at every depth and for hidden and visible senders.
local_checks.result: identifyOwner, decryptSealed, openGroup, openStreamedBundle and decrypt(data:) iterate fetchAllContacts and never read security.currentDepth. The only depth reads in the inbound pipeline are filterShardOperations (OccultaApp.swift:1000-1010), the per-depth challenge slot (ContactManager+ChallengeLedger.swift:74,88,99), importCard's holder test (ContactManager+Cards.swift:288) and the unlock sweeps. A hidden sender's message therefore opens, consumes its prekey and replenishes exactly as at depth 0 (accepted, Bugs 103/104). openGroup returns groupID but nothing stores or displays it, so a group message with partly hidden members shows no member list and no group row is written or read. No error string, viewer element or write differs by sender visibility beyond the accepted rendering.

local_checks.invariant: The message viewer opened from an inbound file offers no reply, compose, contact-detail navigation or other action on the sender.
local_checks.result: The sheet at OccultaApp.swift:450-472 hosts ComposableMessage.Conversation(mode: .read) inside CardFirstMessageFrame. Contact.Info is a plain VStack of name/email/phone with no NavigationLink; the only read-mode actions are Share on a decrypted attachment (ComposableMessage.swift:395-405,449-455,499-503). CardFirstMessageFrame has no button into the contact (comment :10-13, SPEC §ref decided 2026-10-19). Replies and compose are reachable only through the depth-filtered contact list.

local_checks.invariant: A file received while the app is locked is held raw and processed once, at the authenticated depth, whichever unlock path or lowered-lock launch gives access; nothing is written before the PIN.
local_checks.result: handleOpenURL queues any non-.occbak file in pendingFileData when phase != .unlocked (OccultaApp.swift:743-746); AppScreen.phase starts .covered so a cold-launch URL is queued; the .onChange(of: phase) handler drains it after applyVerifyState has set currentDepth (:306-333). With the lock lowered at depth N, Manager.Security.init sets currentDepth = persistedDepth before any view exists, evaluate() goes straight to .unlocked, so a file is processed at depth N by the same code. Source-copy deletion (Bug 101 defer) is depth-independent. A file queued by the real session and drained by a duress PIN is processed at depth N by design (comment :296-305); the consequence is the accepted Bug 103/104 rendering plus a prekey consumed for a message depth 0 then never sees.

local_checks.invariant: Challenge and response handling changes state only in the current depth's slot, writes nothing for a nonce the depth does not hold, and a response to a challenge made at another depth is dropped without a trace.
local_checks.result: route() resolves the sender with fetchContact (no visibility check; renders name, Bug 103/104 accepted) and approvePending can sign for a hidden contact (Bug 173, known). Ledger methods read security.currentDepth themselves; settle() returns before any write when this depth's slot holds a different nonce (:101-103); verifiedBadge reads the current slot only. sweepExpired iterates every contact at every depth and writes only for expired slots, identically at every unlock. A challenge from an unknown sender never reaches the coordinator (error path), so the only new observable is the accepted one. Slot persistence at depth>=1 is the documented Open-ND item (Bug 180 R-items).

local_checks.invariant: Card import at depth N stamps and scopes the contact it creates or changes to depth N, attaches only to contacts visible at N, and shows nothing derived from hidden state beyond decided items.
local_checks.result: importCard creates a new contact through save(contact:currentDepth: security.currentDepth) giving visibleThroughDepth = N and originDepth = N (Contact+Manager.swift:421-429), so it is hidden at every shallower depth including 0. The picker is built from ContactListFilter.visibleContacts (CardImportSheet.swift:204-216) and the same-card holder test is visible-only (ContactManager+Cards.swift:288, CardImportSheet.swift:206), so a hidden holder produces a second contact, by SPEC §6.3. ownIssuedAgreementKeys and redeemCard read every contact at every depth: the own-card refusal (W-18) at a duress depth shows a hidden issued card exists to whoever holds the card file; this is recorded and kept (Docs/Features/Introduction Cards/FINDINGS.md:311, SPEC.md:266). Redemption of a hidden contact's issued card at depth N changes that contact's field and the message renders it, as decided (SPEC §6.6, CardFirstMessageFrame header). recognize() never traps (fixed length, on-curve checks, expiry bounded by 2^53).

local_checks.invariant: Shard operations and custody manifests from a sender hidden at depth N are not applied, and no custody row is written for a hidden owner during a duress session.
local_checks.result: filterShardOperations nils the ops of a hidden or unresolvable sender at both call sites (OccultaApp.swift:1000-1010, :1033-1046, :1152-1165), so distribute, replace and handback are dropped. The custody manifest is passed through unfiltered: processInboundManifest deletes the sender's PendingShardDistribute rows, inserts PotentiallyLostShard watch rows and flips isAbsent (ShardCustody+Manager.swift:291-338), then reconcileBackupPieces runs at depth N. The processing is identical at every depth, rows carry no depth, and statuses are only changed per depth in reconcileBackupPieces, so no depth observable results; recorded as a hardening note because the design text ('every shard op ... a coerced session cannot cause new custody data to be written for a hidden owner') is narrower than the code. Handback banking is depth-blind by design (Vault+Manager+ReturnBuffer.swift header; Bug 99/94).

local_checks.invariant: Contact.Profile.isVisible fails closed for an undecryptable origin or visibility field and applies floor semantics for duress-born contacts.
local_checks.result: isVisible(atDepth:) and the usingKey sibling (Contact+Model.swift:235-262) return false for a present field that will not decrypt or decode, floor semantics for originDepth > 0, ceiling otherwise; both variants agree. nil visibleThroughDepth returns true, documented as an invalid steady state. Callers in the inbound pipeline (filterShardOperations, importCard, CardImportSheet) use it correctly.

hardening: Custody manifests are not run through filterShardOperations (OccultaApp.swift:1033-1046, :1152-1165), so a manifest from a trustee hidden at depth N still deletes PendingShardDistribute rows, inserts PotentiallyLostShard rows and triggers reconcileBackupPieces at depth N (ShardCustody+Manager.swift:291-338). No depth-dependent observable, but filterShardOperations' doc and RECOVERY_BUFFER_LAYERING.md section 2.1 describe the gate as stopping hidden senders from writing custody state; either gate the manifest too (nil it for a hidden sender; it self-corrects on the trustee's next message, RECOVERY_BUFFER_LAYERING.md:372-380) or state in the doc that manifests are deliberately depth-blind.

ContactManager.save(contacts:) and save(contact:) default currentDepth to 0 (Contact+Manager.swift:248-258). The only production callers that rely on the default are the unreachable v1 screens Import+View.swift:187 (struct Import is instantiated only in previews) and Contact+Form.swift:206 (Contacts v1 is not in the tab tree). If either is ever wired in, a contact created at a duress depth is stamped visibleThroughDepth = Int.max, originDepth = 0, i.e. visible at every depth including 0. Make currentDepth a required parameter, or delete the dead screens.

Known and decided, not re-reported: own-card refusal W-18 reveals a hidden issued card to a holder of the card file (FINDINGS.md:311, kept 2026-10-19). Hidden-sender message/challenge rendering (Bugs 103/104), approving a hidden contact's challenge (Bug 173) and per-depth challenge slot residuals (Bug 180) were seen on the same paths and left as is.

A bundle queued while locked and drained by a duress PIN is opened at depth N and consumes its prekey, so the real owner never sees that message. This is the decided consequence of draining identically at both unlock paths (OccultaApp.swift:296-305, Bug 103/104 doc); worth stating in the user guide as a loss mode.

local_checks.invariant: Sealed columns of every Secure Mode model have a constant size whatever the depth or state (claims: pinEnabledPerDepth 29 bytes, DepthCodec 30, VaultEntry/BEK live vs orphaned token one byte, Group slots 156, verifier arrays padded to 32).
local_checks.result: Claims hold against the code: UInt8 encoding of the gate, fixed-width DepthCodec, one-byte sentinels, always-populated deletionToken on VaultEntry/BEK (so no Bug 112 variant there), arrays padded to 32 and Group slots written for all depths together. Remaining keyless variation is lockoutCount (JSON Int, 1 vs 2 digits from 10 attempts) and lockoutAnchor (JSON Double, variable length): both only non-nil after a wrong PIN and not depth-specific (hardening). Known items not re-reported: scalar verifier nil-ness, filler-size mix (Bug 171).

local_checks.invariant: A real unlock and a duress unlock, and an install with and without Secure Mode, write the same rows and do the same checkpoint work.
local_checks.result: Depth-dependent work: draft purge plus one extra checkpoint only when going deeper (applyVerifyState :759-764), purgeUnreadableGroups only at depth 0, sweepPrekeys only for contacts visible at the depth; all other sweeps are all-depth and write only on change; the per-unlock checkpoint is unconditional. Differences are limited to deleted draft rows, a second checkpoint and which contacts' prekeys are swept, which fall under Bug 120 / FTA S10-S11 / Bug 156 (known). AppLayerConfig columns touched by activation (arrays and scalar), configurePIN/disablePIN (persistedDepth, pinEnabledPerDepth[d]) and deactivation (also coercerBaseDepth, scalar to NULL) differ per operation, which is visible only across images (Bug 120 / PR section). Checkpoint result code is ignored and no busy timeout is set (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: Persistent store and keychain artefacts are written at first launch so their existence and dates do not mark Secure Mode use, and the store has no trace outside sealed columns; Erase All Data returns the store to a fresh-install shape.
local_checks.result: Three issues recorded as needs_validation candidates: the secure_delete persistence claim (OccultaApp.swift:160-161), framework bookkeeping outside sealed columns that no code or doc addresses, and Erase All Data deleting the AppLayerConfig row without re-seeding it while re-seeding the BEK and Vault rows. Controls that hold: the Secure Mode Enclave key, the config row and the tier U items are created at launch. The vault Enclave key and r_B are created lazily at the first vault unlock (Key+Manager.swift:899-918), which contradicts the stated goal of LaunchSequence/KeyReseal bootstrapVaultRecord (hardening, not Secure Mode specific).

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate sqlite-secure-delete-header-persistence-claim
local_checks.result: needs_validation: Source confirms the pragma is set only on a throwaway connection, no pragma option reaches SwiftData, and the docs assert header persistence; the iOS runtime fact remains decisive.

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate swiftdata-store-bookkeeping-outside-sealed-columns
local_checks.result: rejected: No code disables or scrubs history, but bugs.md:14996-15004 already documents the history tables and the decided 2.1.0 removal, so it is a known item.

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate erase-all-data-config-row-not-reseeded
local_checks.result: needs_validation: Source confirms the config row is deleted and not re-seeded and Group rows are not deleted, contradicting the stated invariant; impact is low because the wipe already shows itself via deleted keys.

hardening: lockoutCountEncrypted (JSON Int) and lockoutAnchorUptimeEncrypted (JSON Double) have variable sealed length, so a count of 10 or more and the rough magnitude of the uptime anchor are readable without a key; encode both fixed-width like DepthCodec.

Manager.Security.walCheckpoint and OccultaApp.walCheckpoint discard the sqlite3_exec result and set no busy timeout; a BUSY result silently skips the flush that purge, wipe and sweep comments depend on. Check the result and retry.

The vault Enclave key and r_B are created at the first vault unlock (Key+Manager.swift:899-918), so their keychain creation dates mark first vault use, although bootstrapVaultRecord creates the tier B record at launch for exactly that reason.

The depth-deeper path runs checkpointStore twice per unlock (applyVerifyState purge, then the OccultaApp unlock handler) against once for a real unlock; harmless alone but a keyless timing signal in WAL mtimes.

debugPrint/print calls (OccultaApp.swift:1087 and :1147, Contact+Manager.swift:388, PrekeySecretsManager.swift:158 and :278, Features.swift:16) are not stripped in Release; stdout only, no persistent log found.
ComposeViewModel.handleFile copies the user's file into tmp under its original filename (plaintext) until sealed; a kill in that window leaves it until the next launch's tmp sweep.
Orphaned VaultEntry/BEK rows and the 32-row BEK baseline: a BEK row count above 32 needs 32 orphaning cycles, so the keyless count signal is theoretical.

local_checks.invariant: Layer creation never overwrites or exceeds the 32-slot ceiling unnoticed
local_checks.result: writeNormalVerifier/writeDuressVerifier silently drop an index >= 32 (AL:166-179); at depth 31 reEnablePIN writes duress[31], drops normal[32], returns true, so the new PIN is unusable at a cold start; clearVerifiers(from:) would trap on depth > 32 but deactivateSecureMode guards depth < count first (:463). reEnablePIN and activateSecureMode also overwrite an existing layer at N+1 without orphaning its vault entries or BEK (hardening only).

local_checks.invariant: coercerBaseDepth as one persisted value shared by all operators is not an escalation by itself
local_checks.result: Single column (AL:93) read by state (:68) and Settings (:205); writers: activate (:430), reEnablePIN (:982), deactivate (:499). It only widens which depth shows Deactivate; the escalation is in the pop (finding C1). A second operator's reEnablePIN moves the affordance away from the first, which is a UI change visible to the first operator on next use (low).

local_checks.invariant: ContactClassification/saveClassification/setVisibility at depth>0 write only to rows visible at that depth
local_checks.result: saveClassification skips rows with !isVisible(atDepth:) (CM:99); setVisibility fetches by identifier without a visibility guard (CM:124-128) but its only caller (TrustCheckV2.swift:315) passes the open, visible contact. Rows visible at N are rewritten to Int.max or N, which also changes visibility at depths deeper than N (rows classified deeper by another operator are overwritten): hardening, same-direction-of-trust. Hidden rows are untouched. loadSensitiveIDs has no depth guard but isSensitive compares to currentDepth (CC:174-189).

hardening: orphanVaultEntries and orphanBackupKeys return silently when Manager.Ambient.keyManager.createHybridLocalEncryptionKey() fails (Manager+Security.swift:557, 616) after clearVerifiers has already run in the same call; the deactivation then completes with nothing orphaned, so a later layer at that depth inherits the old entries and key. Make deactivation throw before clearing verifiers if the key is unavailable.

VaultEntry.isOrphaned (Vault+Model.swift:825-829) treats a nil or undecryptable deletionToken as orphaned, and the cap loop in orphanVaultEntries (Manager+Security.swift:581-592) hard-deletes the oldest 'orphaned' rows once 50 exist. A live row whose token cannot be read under the current key (for example mid-reseal) would be counted and could be evicted. Consider counting only rows whose token decrypts to the orphaned sentinel.

Operator at the coercerBaseDepth who taps 'Deactivate Protection' lands one depth shallower (Manager+Security.swift:488); at depth 1 that is depth 0 (known question Q1). The vault side of it: sessionID changes, so the vault locks and needs Face ID or the device passcode at depth 0 (OccultaApp.swift:578), which a coercer can compel; no vault-specific gate sits between the landing and the real entries.

A hidden sender's custody manifest is still processed at a duress depth while its shard operations are dropped by filterShardOperations (OccultaApp.swift:1033-1045, 995-1010; ShardCustody+Manager.swift:61-92, 291-330). The dropped operations (a hand-back, a distribute) are consumed with the message and not retried, so the owner can lose a recovery piece if a hidden trustee's message is opened at a depth where it is hidden. Related to known items Bug 103/104 and item 17.

Contact deletion at any depth runs purgeCustody for that contact unconditionally (ShardCustody+Manager.swift:646-696) and the owner's reconcile then marks that trustee lost at depth 0 (OccultaApp.swift:553-559: liveContacts is every non-deleted contact). A contact visible at a duress depth and also a real trustee can be deleted there by whoever holds the unlocked phone. Same family as known item 17; worth stating next to Bug 144.

restoreBackup's early 'depth already has a key' return (Vault+Manager+Backup.swift:408) skips the shard loop and the per-distribution key verification, so a coercer comparing the time to the failure message at depth 0 and at a depth with no key can tell the two apart; the message text is identical at every depth.

VaultEntry.createdAt is a plaintext column on every depth's rows and orders the 50-row eviction (Manager+Security.swift:577-580); it is already recorded (forensic-trace-avoidance.md:196). The eviction order uses a value a restore can set from the backup file (insertEntries :301), so a backup holder chooses which orphaned rows are evicted first; low value, noted for completeness.

excluded_blocks.reason: No HTTP server or client, cookies, OAuth or web auth; the app is offline and serverless.
No webview, DOM or browser storage; the UI is SwiftUI.
No cloud, IAM or deployment infrastructure; SwiftData uses cloudKitDatabase .none.
No model, prompt or agent integration.

local_checks.invariant: Outside-the-store traces (Quick Look extension, pasteboard, keyboard learning, tmp files, print/debugPrint, backup exclusion) reveal no hidden content or Secure Mode use.
local_checks.result: The Quick Look extension is static text (no decryption). Every text input in the app that was counted has autocorrectionDisabled (counts match per file). The pasteboard uses copySensitive (known O2). The store, WAL and SHM are excluded from backup and file-protected. debugPrint calls are not stripped in Release but go to stdout only (hardening). tmp holds plaintext imports for compose until sealed and is cleared at launch (narrow crash window, not depth-specific). No new finding.

hardening: lockoutCountEncrypted (JSON Int) and lockoutAnchorUptimeEncrypted (JSON Double) have variable sealed length, so a count of 10 or more and the rough magnitude of the uptime anchor are readable without a key; encode both fixed-width like DepthCodec.

Manager.Security.walCheckpoint and OccultaApp.walCheckpoint discard the sqlite3_exec result and set no busy timeout; a BUSY result silently skips the flush that purge, wipe and sweep comments depend on. Check the result and retry.

The vault Enclave key and r_B are created at the first vault unlock (Key+Manager.swift:899-918), so their keychain creation dates mark first vault use, although bootstrapVaultRecord creates the tier B record at launch for exactly that reason.

The depth-deeper path runs checkpointStore twice per unlock (applyVerifyState purge, then the OccultaApp unlock handler) against once for a real unlock; harmless alone but a keyless timing signal in WAL mtimes.

debugPrint/print calls (OccultaApp.swift:1087 and :1147, Contact+Manager.swift:388, PrekeySecretsManager.swift:158 and :278, Features.swift:16) are not stripped in Release; stdout only, no persistent log found.
ComposeViewModel.handleFile copies the user's file into tmp under its original filename (plaintext) until sealed; a kill in that window leaves it until the next launch's tmp sweep.
Orphaned VaultEntry/BEK rows and the 32-row BEK baseline: a BEK row count above 32 needs 32 orphaning cycles, so the keyless count signal is theoretical.
